A solid hacking game in the vein of Uplink, Hacker Evolved, etc.  Not breaking new ground, but doing good work within the style.  An adventure game rather than an RPG; there's no currency or upgrades to buy.  Effective graphics, nice music, good effects.  Plays well and is worth the modest price.

Story is thin and poorly told.  Big plot drop at the end, nothing through 2/3 of the game.  Story is predictable and not compelling.  Has a UI problem where the Net map gets clutter quickly and become unusable halfway through the game.

To me, Hacknet really gave me a kind of murder mystery feel. (What happened to Bit?)
It's a puzzle game where you 'hack' your way through a bunch of networks to solve puzzles to eventually find out what happened.
Hack is in quotes, because the one doing the hacking isn't really you, but a bunch of programs you have to find in various places. It doesn't degrade the experience though.

If you're already an experienced hacker, don't expect too much. Otherwise, just enjoy the game.

The price is sat level with the type of game you will play. Don't get me wrong it's very good but expect 10 dollars worth of content. After the main tutorial it kind of just lets you go, if you want you can scan for computers and just look for shit in computers you find but you will eventually reach a dead end and be required to continue the campaign and do missions. The DLC is great and adds a new portsmasher [spoiler] SSLTrojan [/spoiler] as well as a pretty engaging campaign and missions to do. Overall you'll be surprised how fast the hours go by once you get into it. It can be very slightly daunting at first learning commands and such, I myself went into this without any hacking background so it's clear the game doesn't require that. All in all I definitely reccommend it firstly because of how good it is and secondly because of the great pricing. Buy it at full price and most definitely buy it when on sale. tl;dr 9/10 quicktyping
.
Do you like typing? Do you want to test your typing speed? Do you hate online typing sites and/or TyperSh*rk? Do you like tiling window managers? Or do you use Linux?
If you answered "yes" to most of the above questions, then you should get this game. Need more reason? Here's some:
1. Nice story, with some side stories (applicable to both the base game and the DLC).
2. Customizable UI, either by using a provided tool or manually.
3. Some levels require you to think. A lot. While the timer is counting down.
4. There are tons of easter eggs. [spoiler] Shame that the steam codes are already taken [/spoiler]
And here's why you should also get the DLC:
5. New stories, new people, new themes, new tools, some tools can be used as substitutes for others.
6. Your teammates can actually be useful.
7. Some levels require you to [spoiler] actually browse your game directory. Kinda reminds me of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/698780] DDLC [/url] [/spoiler]
8. You can now make your UI a bit tidier.
9. You can also change the music.
There's also a mode(?) called Extensions, in which you can create your own custom storylines. Or you can also browse other people's storylines.
.
Unfortunately, if you don't find any interesting scripts in Extensions, this game has no post-completion contents [spoiler] , assuming you have completed all the trials (Polar Star, Clock, /el, etc etc) [/spoiler] . This is why I wrote "9/10" above.
.

I think the core gameplay is fun, but can be very repetitive. Every time you hack something, you're just launching the same few .exe files and that's it. And a lot of the files when you get into a computer are just placeholder files that are randomly generated.

Would have loved to have seen them expand the idea more with counter-hackers or enforcement agencies getting on your trail to try and arrest you to add more of a penalty for not being careful, with that penalty being a cool cat and mouse thing. But they never really expand on the initial idea outside of a few cool segments.

The reason I'm recommending this is because of those few cool segments. Labyrinth in particular has a very cool segment in the middle that I won't give away that was unlike anything I've ever seen in a game.

And admittedly, it is fun when you get further into the game and you need to actually search for weak-points in network and using that as a point of entry to other systems.

I got this for $3 on sale and I think for what's there is it's worth the full $15 to get the base game and Labyrinth, though maybe $10 for both would be a more accurate value for it.

And after you finish the main game + DLC, there is a lot of good Steam workshop scenarios that have been made so theres plenty of more content for this game beyond the original base game and DLC.

This game is fantastic. The narrative, the branching path, the personality you find with every new character that either helps you or attacks you, the beautiful simplicity of the graphics, the beautiful complexity of the primary gameplay loop. So many good things can be said about this game, while the bad things are honestly so minimal that they're not that noticeable. Unless you somehow find a way to trap yourself and literally cannot progress (which the way around that is just looking up the next step of the quest to cheat your way out of it), there's not much to deter you from your quest. The tension that builds during the tracking countdowns is very well done, with the flashing lights, loud beeping, big red numbers that show every millisecond passing. Speaking of music, the soundtrack is literally good enough to listen to over every other game that I play. The DLC is well worth the price, with adding an entire extra story arc, new hacking options, interesting characters with a very surprising payoff to end it.

Also when you kill the person in the hospital and the music cuts off and it makes you watch as they flatline and all you can hear is the sound of them flatlining is so harrowing 10/10 upgrade your hospital security
